p.fact: Every commit message follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification: a **typed header** and a body that explains *why*.

item.fact: Subject **≤ 60 characters** (hard limit 72), imperative mood, lowercase after the prefix.
`scope` names the **narrowest accurate** subsystem (a crate, package, module, or area).

p.fact: A blank line after the subject, then a free-form body that answers *why*, not *what* — the diff already shows what changed.

item.fact: Never write a subject that summarises *what* changed — write *why*.
Never capitalise the first word after the `type(scope):` prefix, and never omit the type.

p.fact: Conventional Commits is the message **format**; it does not by itself enforce **atomicity** (one commit = one logical idea).
A `feat: add foo, bar, and baz` message is valid Conventional Commits *and* a violation of the atomic rule.
Atomicity is the separate `git-atomic-commits` flow; the two run together.
